transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-16
Start time (UTC): 2027-02-16 15:00
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Redwood Solutions); Maria Lopez (Head of ML, Cobalt Media), Tom Reid (Platform Eng), Sunita Rao (SRE Lead), Ethan Park (Product Manager)

Summary:
- Week 3 POC sync: reviewing model selection matrix, confirming pin policy for traffic, and running an emergency degradation tabletop exercise.
- Discussed tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated for peak burst, fallback models and soft-degrade routing, and required updates to runbook and monitoring.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to produce catalog comparison CSV with latency/cost, Priya to draft emergency swap runbook, customer to share traffic profile.

Topics covered:
- Model matrix review (accuracy vs cost vs latency)
- Pinning policy: hard pin, soft pin, and time-limited pins
- Fallback strategies: shadowing, canary, staged rollback, auto-fallback to smaller model variant
- Observability needs for fast swap: traces, token-level cost, SR (SLO) alarms and audit logs
- Tabletop: simulated failover from ref model (rwd-llama-70b-q4) to fallback (rwd-llama-13b-int8)

Action items (as recorded in call):
- Alex Kim - send catalog comparison CSV + short notes - due 2027-02-18
- Priya Nair - draft emergency swap/runbook (including test checklist) - due 2027-02-19
- Tom Reid - export 7-day traffic distribution and 95/99 latencies - due 2027-02-18

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we wanted to run the weekly sync and then do a quick tabletop on the emergency degrade path, make sure the pin rules line up with your cutover plan.
[00:28] Maria (Cobalt - Head of ML): Yeah sounds good. We ran the last batch of evals overnight, some differences in the long-form summary metric — the 70B variant has better ROUGE but it's about 1.2x the token cost.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Right, and from the service side the 70B q4 path has about 160ms extra median on our dev rig at 2k prompt length distribution, so you'll see that in latency tail too. The KV cache — or K V cash in our logs — is helpful but if you pin hard you won't get the prefix cache wins across minor variants.
[01:12] Tom (Platform Eng): Quick clarifying q: when you say pin hard vs soft pin what does that translate to in routing? Like can we do a soft pin that routes 95% to pinned and 5% to latest?
[01:27] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes you can do weighted soft pin, it's effectively a canary with stable fallback. The policy can be encoded as a route rule: primary model, fallback list, percent for shadowing. If latency climbs above your SLO we can auto-fail to fallback.
[01:45] Maria: Do you have an example of the auto-fail threshold? Is it latency only or also quality regressions?
[01:53] Alex: We typically recommend two triggers: latency breach (95p > X ms for Y minutes) and quality signal (eval on a small sliding prompt set shows degradation beyond threshold). We can wire up alerting to both.
[02:12] Sunita (SRE): On the SLO side we care about 95p and p99 more than median. Also need audit logs for any automatic swap for compliance. SOC 2 folks will want to see who triggered the swap and why.
[02:30] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Noted. We'll include the audit log notes in the runbook.
[02:35] Ethan (PM): One ask — if we do auto-fail to a smaller model, can we preserve response shape for downstream parsers? Some of our infra expects consistent JSON fields.
[02:47] Priya: Good question. We recommend structured output constraints and function-calling style responses — Redwood supports function call emulation and can validate schema at proxy layer. The smaller model sometimes needs prompt engineering to preserve schema; we can add a lightweight response normalizer.
[03:08] Tom: For the tabletop: assume primary is rwd-llama-70b-q4 and fallback rwd-llama-13b-int8. Walk us through steps.
[03:17] Priya: Step one: detect breach — alert fires. Step two: check gating heuristics (is the breach sustained, any partial infra failures?). Step three: execute route change to fallback and disable canary. Step four: run smoke tests (5 canonical prompts) and monitor. If smoke passes, keep fallback and open incident for postmortem. If smoke fails, revert to prior pinned model or open manual escalation.
[03:48] Maria: How fast is that route change? Seconds, minutes?
[03:53] Priya: For hosted routes it's typically sub-30s to push policy and start routing. For dedicated pools with pinned capacity it can be near-instant if both models are warm; if fallback needs spin-up it might be 2-5 minutes. We also discussed pre-warming fallback to avoid cold start.
[04:15] Tom: For our traffic pattern — bursty marketing flows at 30 TPS for short windows — pre-warm cost is a concern. If we keep both warm it's expensive.
[04:27] Alex: That's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. Redwood Optimize can give an expected unit-cost delta if you keep a small reserved pool for the fallback. We'll put numbers in the CSV.
[04:40] Maria: Another constraint: data residency. Some user content must stay in EU region and your private deployment was discussed earlier. Does the fallback honor region constraints?
[04:53] Priya: Yes, routing policies can be region-constrained. In Private deployments you control the hardware so fallback in-region is a requirement — we can show a matrix of supported model variants by region in the catalog sheet.
[05:10] Sunita: Regarding audit and KMS: if we do an emergency swap does the key material change or does it remain under our KMS?
[05:18] Alex: For Private and Dedicated deployments, keys remain under your KMS/HSM. For hosted we can integrate with your KMS for volume encryption and request-level encryption per contract. We'll add a note.
[05:34] Maria: Let's run the tabletop scenario — we'll simulate a 95p breach from 480ms to 900ms over 7 minutes.
[05:42] Priya: Ok step one alert triggers. [crosstalk] Who's owning the smoke runner?
[05:50] Tom: We can run the smoke runner from our stage infra, we'll need the fallback endpoint info and a small script.
[06:00] Alex: I'll provide the endpoint and a minimal test harness. Priya will provide the canonical prompt set.
[06:08] [15:12] Speaker 2: umm right the transcription jumped here a bit (auto note)
[06:20] Priya: For the smoke tests create 5 canonical prompts that exercise the long-form summarize, the product-rewrite and the bullet extraction — that will catch schema regressions.
[06:33] Maria: If smoke fails do we automatically revert or open manual?
[06:38] Priya: Our recommended default is manual revert after auto-fail unless you set a safe automatic escape hatch that reverts after N minutes if quality doesn't meet threshold. That reduces flip-flopping risk.
[06:50] Sunita: We'll want explicit guardrails: no automatic revert without an on-call ack for the first 48 hours after swap.
[06:58] Alex: We can codify that in the runbook as a policy option.
[07:05] Ethan: Are there any known QA regressions when going from 70B -> 13B int8? We've seen hallucination uptick in other vendors.
[07:14] Priya: You're right, smaller models tend to shorten factual grounding. We recommend a fallback prompt layer that enforces source citations where possible and a regression evaluation set. Also can route certain prompt classes to the 70B only — e.g., responses with high factuality needs.
[07:34] Tom: Implementation question: how does the version pin interact with your rollout UI? Can we unpin from the UI or only via API?
[07:43] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Both. UI supports pin/unpin and you can set soft pin weights; API is best for automations. We'll share UI screenshots in the follow-up.
[07:55] Maria: One more ask — do you publish deterministic compatibility notes? We had issues where tokenization changed between minor variants.
[08:03] Priya: We'll add a tokenization compatibility column in the catalog sheet. Some minor variant tokenizers are identical but quantization paths can change token streaming behaviors — we'll flag those.
[08:19] Alex: Wrapping up let's confirm owners. Alex will send the comparison CSV, Priya the runbook, Tom the traffic dump. Any other items?
[08:28] Maria: We'll also run a small stress bench against the fallback if you can provide endpoints.
[08:33] Alex: Yes we'll provide.
[08:36] [48:00] End of recorded transcribed portion — remaining 4 minutes included Q&A off the record
